caption: Analytics in the Main menu
preconditions: Instance has superdesk-analytics installed and enabled (server INSTALLED_APPS contains 'analytics'; client superdesk.config.js has 'superdesk.analytics' in apps and 'superdesk-analytics' in importApps). The current demo stack does NOT have it; use an Analytics-enabled build such as the default superdesk host build on develop.
Logged in as admin (all privileges, including every 'Analytics - ...' privilege)
steps: Open #/workspace/monitoring and wait for [data-test-id="top-menu"]
Wait for [data-test-id="main-menu"] to be visible and for [data-test-id="main-menu-item"][data-test-value="Analytics"] to exist
Hover [data-test-id="main-menu-item"][data-test-value="Analytics"]
notes: Analytics is registered as a main-menu activity (category MENU_MAIN, adminTools false), so it is listed in the upper group of the Hamburger Menu, not under 'Admin tools'. It only appears when the user has at least one report privilege.

caption: A Content Publishing report, grouped by category
preconditions: Instance has superdesk-analytics installed and enabled (server INSTALLED_APPS contains 'analytics'; client superdesk.config.js has 'superdesk.analytics' in apps and 'superdesk-analytics' in importApps). notes: Shows the whole page: top bar, report panel on Parameters, and the column chart. The default chart type is Column.

ANALYTICS_ENABLE_ARCHIVE_STATS = True and archive statistics generated after the seed content was created: run `python manage.py analytics:gen_archive_statistics` in the server container (the hourly celery beat job is too slow for a capture run)
Desk 'Politics' had items created, fetched, sent in and out, published and spiked over the last 7 days (the seed script should spread history over several days and hours)
steps: Open #/analytics?report=desk_activity_report and wait for .sd-filters-panel
In 'Desk' select 'Politics'
In 'Interval' select 'Daily'
In 'Date Filter:' select 'Relative Days' and pick '7 days'
Wait for the chart (svg.highcharts-root) and the table below it (.sda-chart__table) to render
notes: Needs archive statistics; without them the report is not in the list. The table has the Incoming (Total, Create, Fetch, Duplicate, Sent To, Deschedule, Unspike) and Outgoing (Total, Publish, Spike, Sent From, Publish Scheduled, Publish Embargo) column groups; make the viewport tall enough to show both chart and table.

ANALYTICS_ENABLE_ARCHIVE_STATS = True and archive statistics generated after the seed content was created: run `python manage.py analytics:gen_archive_statistics` in the server container (the hourly celery beat job is too slow for a capture run)
Yesterday, user 'editor' (or another named user) opened, edited and closed 5 to 8 different items at different times of day, so the timeline has several rows
steps: Open #/analytics?report=user_activity_report and wait for .sd-filters-panel
In 'User' search for and pick the seeded user
Under 'Date Filter:' ('Single Day') pick yesterday's date
Wait for the xrange chart (svg.highcharts-root) with sluglines on the y axis
Click the first bar in the chart and wait for the second chart (#item_timeline_report) to render and scroll into view
Scroll back so both charts are visible if the viewport allows
notes: Bars are periods during which the user had the item locked (item_lock to item_unlock in archive history), so the seed must lock and unlock items as that user, not only create them. If both charts do not fit, capture the first chart only and say so in the capture log.

caption: Scheduling a report by email
preconditions: Instance has superdesk-analytics installed and enabled (server INSTALLED_APPS contains 'analytics'; client superdesk.config.js has 'superdesk.analytics' in apps and 'superdesk-analytics' in importApps). The current demo stack does NOT have it; use an Analytics-enabled build such as the default superdesk host build on develop.
Logged in as admin (all privileges, including every 'Analytics - ...' privilege)

ANALYTICS_ENABLE_ARCHIVE_STATS = True and archive statistics generated after the seed content was created: run `python manage.py analytics:gen_archive_statistics` in the server container (the hourly celery beat job is too slow for a capture run)

A global saved report for Desk Activity named 'Politics desk, last 7 days' exists (desk Politics, interval Daily, Relative Days 7). Create it via POST /api/saved_reports {name, report: 'desk_activity_report', params: {...}, is_global: true} or through the UI
Users with email addresses exist (e.g. editor@example.com) so the To: field can pick them
steps: Open #/analytics?report=desk_activity_report and wait for .sd-filters-panel
Wait for .saved-reports and the item 'Politics desk, last 7 days' under 'Global Saved Reports'
Wait for the modal .modal.scheduled-reports (heading 'Edit "" Schedule')
Turn on 'Active'; Name: 'Politics desk weekly'; Description: 'Sent every Monday morning'
When: select 'Weekly', pick hour '8:00am', tick 'MO'
In 'To:' pick the editor user and type one external address, e.g. desk-chief@example.com
Subject: 'Politics desk activity, last 7 days'; Format: 'PDF File'; leave Image Width at 800 pixels
notes: Do not click Create. The modal heading reads 'Edit "<name>" Schedule' even for a new schedule (it uses the typed name), which is why a name is typed before the capture. Weekday checkboxes appear only for 'Weekly'. If the crop selector .modal__content does not match the sd-modal markup, crop to the element with class 'scheduled-reports'.
